  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Francisco Giants, 6:45p

Summary

This one's near the top of the watchability charts today, and deservedly so: a red-hot Brewers club with a dominant bullpen taking on a Giants team that keeps overachieving its underlying numbers. Milwaukee sits atop the NL Central at 66-40 after a strong homestand, bringing the show to Old Friend Willy Adames and the Giants to open a West Coast trip — a nice subplot given Adames spent years anchoring Milwaukee's infield before signing in San Francisco. The Brewers' 9.00 tNERD is driven by an excellent bullpen, quality baserunning, and a young, cheap roster, while the Giants' still-solid 4.66 mark leans heavily on Oracle Park broadcast charm and a notable "positive luck" gap — meaning San Francisco (45-61) has actually been playing worse than its record indicates. On the mound, 24-year-old Logan Henderson is the headliner, with a 4-1 record, 3.05 ERA, 0.94 WHIP and elite peripherals (9.92 pNERD, well above today's 5.78 average) built on excellent strike-throwing and whiff rates. Landen Roupp counters capably, with a 7-8 record, 3.93 ERA, and 113 strikeouts, giving this game a legitimately compelling top-of-scale gNERD of 15.00.

Cleveland Guardians @ Cincinnati Reds, 4:10p

Summary

A frontline arm carrying a middling supporting cast is the story here, with Cleveland's Gavin Williams doing enough heavy lifting to make this one worth your remote. Williams' pNERD of 11.50 sits near the top of both today's slate and the broader season sample, built on a hard-to-square combination of premium velocity (97 mph average) and elite contact suppression (xFIP- of 72). The Reds' counterpart is officially unnamed, which is its own small mystery, though Cincinnati's lineup gives him little help either way — Cincinnati's tNERD of 4.11 reflects a club with shaky batting and fielding runs, and they'll be doing it without Steer, who's headed for the injured list after a right wrist injury expected to cost "significant time". Cleveland's offense isn't exactly thriving either — the Guardians have been shut out in their last two games and scored just four runs in their last four — but their 7.16 tNERD, boosted by strong baserunning and bullpen work, still clears the Reds comfortably. Not a marquee slugfest, but Williams alone makes this worth checking in on.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

A middling pitching matchup wrapped around a genuinely fun, feisty young Marlins team makes this one worth a look, even if neither starter is a must-watch arm. Nola is in the middle of the worst season of his career, having allowed more home runs (25) than any pitcher in the National League this season, though his pNERD (5.16) gets a boost from positive luck, suggesting his ugly ERA overstates how bad he's been. Alcantara, Miami's most reliable starter this season, regularly working into the seventh inning, brings real velocity (97.5 mph, best among today's starters) but is coming off one of his worst starts of the year in allowing 5 ER last Wednesday. The real draw is Miami's tNERD of 9.82 — comfortably above today's 5.63 average — fueled by a young, cheap, and lucky roster that's overperforming its baseline, even while stuck in a brutal 1-9 slide. Toss in a legitimate NL East rivalry, a season series the Phillies lead 5-3, and a gNERD of 13.08 that clears today's average, and this is a solidly above-average watch, powered more by team quirkiness than pitching brilliance.

Atlanta Braves @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

Chris Sale, at 37, is pitching like it's 2018 again, and that alone makes this worth a look even though the Mets are limping toward the finish line. Sale enters with an eye-catching mark of dominance: Atlanta turns to its ace, Chris Sale, with an eye on evening the series, and Sale has once again been one of the National League's most dominant starters. His 9.02 pNERD is well above today's average and reflects elite whiff and strike rates paired with a still-lively fastball, though his deliberate pace docks him slightly. Across town, Christian Scott — a return act himself after Tommy John/internal-brace surgery wiped out his 2025 — has quietly turned into a solid five-and-dive arm; the Mets counter with Christian Scott, who has quietly put together a strong season, allowing just 21 earned runs since the start of May. The Mets lineup is shorthanded too: Sale's combination of strikeout volume and command is especially lethal against a team missing Juan Soto and Mark Vientos from its everyday lineup. The gNERD of 13.05 sits comfortably above both the historical median and today's slate average, mostly thanks to Sale's arm and a Mets broadcast crew that punches above its weight in the tNERD math. Watch for the pitching, not the scoreboard — this profiles as a lopsided, strikeout-heavy affair rather than a slugfest.

New York Yankees @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

Gerrit Cole's return from Tommy John surgery has been the best kind of baseball theater, and pairing his revival with a scrappy young White Sox club makes this one worth carving out time for. Cole, who missed all of 2025 and the first two months of this season, has looked essentially unslowed since his May comeback—his fastball touched 99.6 mph in his season debut against the Rays, and three starts into the season he was sitting on a 2.00 ERA and 0.89 WHIP. That track record shows up in his pNERD of 7.32, built on plus velocity, elite strike-throwing, and a tidy xFIP-. His counterpart, Anthony Kay, is the clear name-value gap here: a 1.23 pNERD reflects below-average command and strikeout stuff, so don't expect a duel. The real juice comes from the lineups—both the Yankees (8.85 tNERD) and White Sox (8.59 tNERD) rank well above the historical average of 5.23, with New York's power/baserunning combo and Chicago's young, cheap roster both flashing well above league norms. Add it up and you get a 13.00 gNERD, solidly above today's 11.31 average and comfortably in the upper half of games historically—watch for Cole's stuff even if Kay struggles to keep pace.

Cleveland Guardians @ Cincinnati Reds, 10:40a

Summary

Chase Burns is the reason to tune in here—a 23-year-old righty humming 97.8 mph with swing-and-miss stuff that's turned into a legitimate NL Cy Young case, and he's carrying a pNERD of 9.85, comfortably above today's slate average. Burns brings a 12-1 record and a tidy xFIP- of 84 into a matchup against a Guardians lineup that's been shut out in back-to-back games and owns one of baseball's worst offenses, so don't expect much resistance. Cleveland countering with Slade Cecconi is more of a mixed bag—his 3.33 pNERD reflects a pitcher who posted a 1.88 ERA in five June starts but has allowed 15 runs on 22 hits in July. The gNERD of 12.23 lands above both the historic average and today's 11.31 mean, propped up largely by Cleveland's tNERD of 7.16—young, cheap, and running well on the bases—versus Cincinnati's thinner 4.11, hurt by a shaky bullpen and a lineup missing regulars to injury. Add in José Ramírez still shaking off rust after a hamate fracture, and this one's watchable mostly for Burns' dominance rather than for drama.

Baltimore Orioles @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Melton has been sharp lately (three earned runs allowed over his last six starts) while Kremer just got roughed up by Boston, allowing a season-high six runs. He's also coming back from injury. There's plenty of concrete storylines here.

A rookie-caliber arm with electric stuff against a veteran trying to find his footing again makes this the more watchable half of this Baltimore-Detroit set. Troy Melton, the Tigers' 25-year-old righty, owns a 1.95 ERA on the season and has held opponents to two runs or less over his last six games, posting a 1.31 ERA and 3.08 FIP over that stretch while striking out 41. His 7.39 pNERD, built on mid-90s velocity and a quick pace, sits comfortably above today's average. Kremer, by contrast, is scuffling — he gave up a season-high six runs in his latest start, four of them in the first inning against Boston, though he managed to hang around for six innings. His 6.62 pNERD is buoyed mostly by lucky/xFIP components rather than results, and he missed more than two months with a right quad strain before returning. The Orioles offense has been rolling — Coby Mayo hit a two-run homer and drove in three, while Jackson Holliday delivered a four-hit game in Monday's win — but both bullpens are middling and the gNERD of 11.69 lands just above the historical median, buoyed almost entirely by pitching intrigue rather than lineup firepower.

Boston Red Sox @ Athletics, 6:40p

Summary

A dud on paper, but the pitching says otherwise—this is a sneaky-solid arms race wearing an ugly team-record costume. The Red Sox are just fine (5.43 tNERD, roughly average) while the A's rank near the bottom of the league in tNERD (2.91), and it shows: Oakland/Sacramento is on a three-game losing skid and hitting a paltry .230 as a team over their last ten games. Their calling card is bad defense and a shaky bullpen dragging down otherwise passable offense from Soderstrom and Gelof.

The pitching is the actual draw. Jake Bennett (7.16 pNERD) is young, was efficient, and pounds the zone. Gage Jump (7.40 pNERD) throws hard for his age but comes in shaky—he gave up six earned runs and allowed eight hits in 4 2/3 innings against Arizona in his last start. Combined, both arms clear the 95th percentile for pitcher NERD today, giving this game a gNERD of 11.45—above the historical average and squarely mid-pack among today's slate. Watch for the arms, not the standings.

Texas Rangers @ Tampa Bay Rays, 3:40p

Summary

A solidly above-average matchup thanks to a genuinely nasty Rays starter, even if the Rangers' side of the probable-pitcher ledger is a mystery.   • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Philadelphia Phillies @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Zack Wheeler is quietly having one of the better seasons in baseball and Miami is in full collapse mode—that combination makes this worth your evening. The Marlins have dropped 12 straight games, a franchise record, and have yet to win since the All-Star break. Wheeler counters that misery by walking in with a sparkling 10-2 record and a 2.16 ERA, backed by an xFIP- of just 65 and elite swinging-strike rate that push his pNERD to 9.09, comfortably above today's average. Chicago Cubs @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 10:35a

Summary

A dominant Ashcraft strikeout arm meets a Cubs offense riding a 31-run scoring binge, making this the day's most watchable matchup on paper. At 15.67, today's gNERD sits well above both the historic average (10.11) and today's slate average (11.32), and it's driven mostly by a lopsided pitching matchup: Braxton Ashcraft's 11.58 pNERD (elite xFIP-, 97 mph heat, brisk pace) dwarfs Jameson Taillon's modest 3.97. That said, Ashcraft's last outing saw him give up seven earned runs in three innings against the Yankees, so buyer beware on recent form even as his skills grade out well. The Pirates enter having Pittsburgh hosting the Cubs while riding a three-game losing skid and are trying to avoid a series sweep. Both offenses carry real juice—Chicago's tNERD (8.49) and Pittsburgh's (7.30) both rank comfortably above the historic 75th percentile—with Pete Crow-Armstrong pacing Chicago in OBP (.390) and slugging (.544) and Bryan Reynolds anchoring Pittsburgh. Add in Taillon's history as a former Pirate first-round product returning to PNC Park, and there's enough juice here to make this the pick of the day.

Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski is must-watch theater against a Rockies team that has no business being in this ballpark, and the numbers back that up as strongly as anything on today's slate. Misiorowski, the 24-year-old flamethrower who's become a genuine Cy Young conversation piece, leads the majors with 173 strikeouts and in ERA, and he consistently hits 100 mph or more on the radar gun. His pNERD of 15.00 is essentially maxed out, driven by elite whiff rates, a microscopic xFIP-, and velocity that sits near the top of the league — this is as close to appointment viewing as a start gets. Opposite him, Kyle Freeland has been scuffling, having lost his last two decisions, allowing four runs over six innings in both outings, though his pNERD of 5.37 is respectable thanks to strong control and some rough luck. The Brewers' 8.87 tNERD (driven by baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young, boosted lineup) dwarfs Colorado's league-worst 1.41, with Milwaukee's rookies Cooper Pratt and Luis Lara instrumental in Saturday night's 8-5 Milwaukee win. At 15.32, this gNERD ranks near the top of both today's games and the historical distribution — mostly on the strength of one dominant arm.

New York Yankees @ Philadelphia Phillies, 4:20p

Summary

I've got enough to write a solid summary now.

Watch this one for Sánchez alone — a legitimate Cy Young-caliber arm against a Yankees lineup that leads baseball in team ERA, with the Phillies trying to snap a home skid. Cristopher Sánchez brings a 10.21 pNERD, driven by an absurd 61 xFIP-, elite swinging-strike rate, and plus velocity — this is a top-shelf starter having a genuinely dominant season. This is his 22nd start of the season, and the 29-year-old carries a 2.65 ERA with a 6.04 strikeout-to-walk ratio. That said, July has been rough for him, with a 7.47 ERA and 1.98 WHIP across 16 innings, plus a jump in barrel rate — worth watching whether he's settling back in. Opposite him, Will Warren (4.33 pNERD) is a more pedestrian arm, prone to traffic on the bases, though he's shown flashes of getting outs when it matters. The Yankees' 8.54 tNERD is the headline offensive story here — strong barrel rates, baserunning, and bullpen — while Philadelphia's 5.34 leans more on baserunning and pen depth than its middling bat. Philadelphia sits at 27-27 at home and 38-5 when scoring five-plus runs, so a quiet Phillies bat could make this lopsided fast. At 14.21 gNERD, this ranks comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — a good pick.

Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

A rare treat: this is the day's best watch, headlined by a legit ace-versus-ace pitching duel with actual stakes attached. Paul Skenes brings a 10.25 pNERD—tops among today's slate—built on elite xFIP- and a 96.9 mph heater, and even though his surface numbers have wobbled lately (a 4.93 ERA in his last seven starts, "nearly a run and a half higher than his three-year career mark"), the underlying stuff still grades out excellent. Across from him, Shota Imanaga (5.93 pNERD) has quietly caught fire, posting a 1.62 ERA over three July starts and threw seven scoreless innings last time out. Both clubs bring real thump: the Cubs' 8.29 tNERD leans on standout fielding and batting runs, while Pittsburgh's 7.44 mixes strong baserunning with a payroll-underdog appeal. The two teams are tied 4-4 in the season series, and with both teams carrying genuine postseason ambitions, the Cubs at 58-45 clinging to a wild-card spot and Pittsburgh right on the edge of that conversation, there's context to match the talent. At 15.96, the gNERD score sits well above both the historic 95th percentile (14.76) and today's average (11.06)—about as good as it gets.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ New York Mets, 4:15p

Summary

Good pitchers' duel — the Dodgers' ace against the Mets' emerging rookie phenom, and both are dealing right now. Yamamoto and McLean actually met once before this season in a tight April duel, and this rematch has real juice: Yamamoto is coming off a pedestrian 3.60 ERA as recently as May 12 before pitching to a 2.20 mark over 10 starts, including his last outing, a complete-game two-run performance. McLean, meanwhile, has been quietly dominant, with a 0.75 ERA over his last four starts, including an active streak of 17 consecutive innings without an earned run, built on a new approach of lasting at least six innings in six straight starts by peppering the strike zone with four-seamers and sinkers early in counts rather than his breaking stuff. Both pitchers grade out well above average here — McLean edges Yamamoto slightly thanks to youth and a quicker pace, and their near-identical xFIP- marks confirm this isn't just ERA magic. The Dodgers bring by far the day's best offense, riding a 65-38 record, while the Mets counter with a middling lineup — but that pitching matchup alone makes this one of the stronger watches on the board, well above both the historical and today's average gNERD marks.

San Diego Padres @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

A rare high-end matinee: young flamethrower Eury Pérez against a lineup that's finally waking up, in a game that ranks near the top of both today's slate and the season overall. This one carries a gNERD of 14.31, comfortably above the historic median and near the upper end of today's games, driven almost entirely by two well-rounded, entertaining teams rather than a marquee pitching duel. Pérez is the story here — the 23-year-old is carrying a 1.14 ERA over his past seven starts, most recently allowing one hit over six shutout innings against Milwaukee, and his 98 mph heat and elite swinging-strike rate back up a strong 7.91 pNERD. Sears, by contrast, sits at a modest 1.99 pNERD — he's bounced back in July with a 2.51 ERA in three starts after a rough start to his Padres tenure, but the peripherals (poor strike-throwing, plodding pace) suggest he's more innings-eater than headliner. Where this game earns its keep is on the position-player side: both clubs grade out near 9.5 tNERD, with Miami's young, cheap, feisty roster and San Diego's baserunning/bullpen/fielding combo giving this the look of two frisky underdogs — San Diego's lineup has averaged 6.71 runs per game since the break, including a 19-run outburst, despite going just 2-5 over that span. Worth tuning in for the contrast alone.

Seattle Mariners @ Texas Rangers, 4:15p

Summary

I have enough information from the searches already gathered to write a solid, specific summary.

Two of the best pitchers in baseball this year face off in a game that means real division standings, not just style points. Bryan Woo and Nathan Eovaldi both grade out among the more effective starters, and the Rangers-Mariners series carries genuine stakes in a scrambled AL West race.

This is a rematch of an ongoing AL West battle where the AL West has been wide open all season, with the Rangers clinging to a half-game lead in first place while the Mariners are eager to re-establish their position as division favorites. Seattle arrives in a funk — still searching for answers after a rough loss to the Reds, with the trade deadline approaching and this series carrying real weight on how the team approaches upgrading the roster — while the Rangers lead the season series 4-2, meaning anything more than a split would give them the tiebreaker if the race comes down to September.

The pitching is the real draw. Eovaldi's xFIP- of 79 and elite swinging-strike rate power a pNERD near 8.4, while Woo backs him with plus velocity and command for a 7.66 mark — both well above today's average of 5.52 and comfortably in the upper quartile of the historic range. Texas's tNERD (6.06) outpaces Seattle's shaky, error-prone unit (2.69, dragged down by weak fielding and baserunning), though the Rangers' outsized batting luck (+34, one of the highest values you'll see) suggests some regression could be coming. Combined, the 12.38 gNERD sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — a solid, quietly compelling pitchers' duel wrapped in postseason-race tension.

Dylan Cease's arm alone makes this worth a look, even if the Blue Jays around him have gone ice-cold. Cease brings elite swing-and-miss stuff to Fenway, and the underlying gap between Toronto's tNERD (2.07) and Boston's tNERD (6.04) tells the real story: this is a middling offense club facing a Boston squad that fields it well and gets more from its bullpen, even while missing key pieces.

Cease's pNERD of 10.23 is the headline here — Dylan Cease enters at 6-5 with a 2.67 ERA, a 1.14 WHIP and 155 strikeouts over 104.1 innings, backed by a filthy xFIP- and mid-90s heat that should keep this watchable even if Toronto's lineup keeps sleepwalking. Sonny Gray, by contrast, checks in with a modest 4.01 pNERD; his stuff has ticked down and his pace is glacial, though his command remains sharp enough that Boston has hit .245 over its past 23 with a .421 slugging percentage behind him. Summary

The Reds and Cardinals aren't tNERD powerhouses—Cincinnati sits below average on offense and bullpen while St. Louis leans on youth and steady fielding—but the real hook here is Greene, who's still finding his footing after having bone chips removed from his throwing elbow during Spring Training, with a projected recovery timeline of around four months. Since returning, he's been wildly inconsistent, swinging between an eight-run clunker and a dominant seven-scoreless-inning, 12-strikeout performance, which is exactly the kind of boom-or-bust unpredictability that makes a start worth tuning into even without reliable NERD data (his pNERD reads zero simply because we lack a sample). Pallante, by contrast, is the steadier hand—a 95-mph-plus sinkerballer with playable peripherals backing a 3.93 pNERD. Cincinnati arrives on a three-game win streak despite sitting last in the NL Central, while St. Louis's younger, cheaper roster and strong glovework nudge their tNERD to a decent 6.01. Overall gNERD of 9.62 lands a bit below the historical average, making this a watch-if-curious rather than must-see slot on today's slate.

A middling AL Central afternoon with a genuine trade-deadline subplot: this is Casey Mize possibly making his last start in a Tigers uniform. With the deadline days away, Detroit's impending free agent has quietly been one of the better stories in this series—he's battled groin tightness at various times this season, but when he's been on the mound, he has delivered quality innings, allowing two or fewer runs in 11 of his 15 starts. His pNERD of 6.40 backs that up, built on a strong xFIP- and above-average swinging-strike rate. Wacha, at 4.19 pNERD, is a solid complementary arm—though he's had a rough July, posting a 5.91 ERA and 5.36 FIP over his last three starts—but he does own a history of tormenting Detroit, including a scoreless outing earlier this year. Team-wise, neither club is thrilling: Kansas City's bullpen is a genuine sinkhole (tNERD 2.77), while Detroit's 4.77 gets a boost mostly from barrel rate and some broadcast polish. The 9.06 gNERD lands below the historic middle and today's average, so temper expectations, but the Mize storyline and both pitchers' recent quality starts give this some juice beyond the raw numbers.

Summary

Both teams are near the bottom of their divisions with little to play for, and the pitching matchup does little to change that. The pitching matchup is lopsided in theory but shaky in practice. Rookie Ryan Johnson, just 23, is set to oppose Ray after facing four batters in relief and retiring them all in his only previous meeting with the Giants, on April 19, 2025. He's coming off five innings of one-run ball in a 3-2 win over the Detroit Tigers, and his 5.00 pNERD (age and some swinging-strike upside) is actually the better of the two arms today. Robbie Ray, meanwhile, carries a career highlight reel but a pedestrian 1.01 pNERD, with a below-average strike rate dragging things down; he's coming off a no-decision Sunday after yielding three runs on seven hits in four-plus innings against the Mariners. On the plus side, Ray is 3-1 with a 2.53 ERA in five career starts against the Angels, so there's a track record worth noting even if the era's peripherals suggest regression toward mediocrity. The Giants' team profile gets a boost mostly from lousy recent luck (suggesting some positive regression ahead) and above-average broadcast ratings, but neither roster's underlying metrics — fielding, baserunning, bullpen — give much reason to tune in. File this one under "background noise" unless you're rooting for laundry.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Minnesota Twins @ Cleveland Guardians, 10:10a

Summary

Cleveland's had this Twins series circled all week, and the last game of a four-game set arrives with the Guardians already up 2-1 and both starters carrying real swing-and-miss stuff. Gavin Williams headlines the day: his 11.10 pNERD is comfortably above today's average and sits in rare territory historically, powered by a strong xFIP (74, well better than league average) and elite strikeout/whiff numbers. Williams owns a 2.39 xFIP over the last 30 days, which does not align with his 4.70 ERA, and this looks like a good matchup for the numbers to finally catch up. That underperformance shows up in his positive luck component, suggesting better results than his ERA lately would indicate. Taj Bradley isn't chopped liver either, with a 6.87 pNERD boosted by mid-90s-plus velocity, though Bradley holds a clear edge against this specific opponent, owning a 1.54 ERA in four career starts versus the Guardians, including a 10-strikeout outing over seven innings on July 7. On the team side, Cleveland's 7.73 tNERD (aided by a young, inexpensive roster and a strong bullpen) dwarfs Minnesota's underwhelming 2.37, and Cleveland has outscored Minnesota 28-12 across the first three games of this series. With a gNERD of 14.03 - well above both the historical and today's averages - this is one of the more watchable matchups on the board, thanks almost entirely to the pitching.

Detail

New York Mets @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Good. The Brewers lead the NL Central at 63-37/38, the best record in the National League, while the Mets sit well below .500 on the road. Both starters are having strong seasons, with Henderson working on a limited pitch/innings count and Scott coming off dominant back-to-back starts.

The Brewers' best-in-the-NL record meets a Mets club playing out the string, but the pitching matchup makes this worth a look anyway. Milwaukee enters at the National League Central at 63-37, the best record in the senior circuit, while New York limps in having gone 22-31 in road games and 43-59 overall. That imbalance shows up in the tNERD gap—Brewers 8.34 to the Mets' 4.23—Milwaukee's young, cheap, athletic roster (lowest average age, strong baserunning and bullpen marks) contrasting with a Mets team whose big-money roster hasn't hit or run the bases well this year. The pitching is the real draw. Logan Henderson, just 24, has been outstanding: a 2.45 ERA, 2.84 FIP, and 71 strikeouts over 58 2/3 innings across his brief career, and his 8.85 pNERD ranks near the top of today's slate. Christian Scott isn't far behind, riding 10 2/3 innings with no runs allowed and 12 strikeouts against the Royals and Phillies in his last two outings. Both are first-time opponents for each other, adding a little novelty. At 13.69, the gNERD comfortably clears today's average of 10.44, making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board despite the standings gap.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ New York Yankees, 10:05a

Summary

Good storylines found. Now let me write the summary.

Cole against his old team is the headline, and the underlying numbers back it up as a genuinely solid watch. Gerrit Cole draws Pittsburgh — the franchise that drafted him first overall 15 years ago — in the opener of a rain-forced doubleheader, and he's been mostly excellent since returning from last spring's Tommy John surgery. His 6.06 pNERD is comfortably above average, driven by strong strike-throwing and velocity that's actually ticked up to 96.8 mph; the only blemish has been a recent tendency to serve up homers, with eight home runs allowed already, a number Cole and the Yankees are watching closely. Mitch Keller is more of a middling stopgap here (3.30 pNERD), held back by unremarkable swing-and-miss stuff, though positive pitching luck suggests his results have actually undersold his stuff. Where this game earns its 13.06 gNERD — comfortably above both the historical average and today's slate — is the lineups: both Pittsburgh and New York rank near the top of the league in barrel rate and baserunning value, and the Yankees' 8.86 tNERD is buoyed by strong bullpen and contact-quality metrics. A well-rounded, above-average game worth carving out time for.

The Red Sox are riding the hottest streak in baseball and Fenway smells like history in the making. Boston has won 14 straight and sits one victory from tying the franchise record for consecutive wins, a run that stands as the longest in Major League Baseball this season and the longest in the majors since the Brewers won 14 in a row last August. Lefty Jake Bennett draws the assignment, and it's uncharted territory for both sides since Bennett is facing the Orioles for the first time. His pNERD of 7.02 is legitimately strong, built on plus strike-throwing and a tidy pace, and at 25 he's exactly the kind of prospect worth watching build a track record in real time. Dean Kremer counters with a 6.31 pNERD boosted heavily by good fortune — his ERA-beating xFIP gap accounts for most of his score, so some regression could be lurking. Boston's tNERD (6.27) edges Baltimore's (4.74), powered by strong fielding and bullpen work, while the Orioles counter with modest pop and Baltimore's own quieter three-city-comparable run of form. At 12.17, the gNERD sits comfortably above the historical average and this season's daily average, making it a solidly above-average watch, streak drama included.

Team-wise, neither club stands out — Arizona's tNERD (4.63) edges Oakland's (3.50), with the Diamondbacks propped up by strong fielding and baserunning against a lineup that's been quietly punchless. Overall gNERD of 8.61 sits below both the historic and today's averages, making Jump's continued development the real reason to watch.

Cleveland has won three straight in this set, and Guardians closer Cade Smith just notched his 29th save while Byron Buxton made a highlight-caliber throw that nearly ended a Cleveland rally before replay reversed it.

On the mound, Bailey Ober is quietly the more interesting story: in his last two starts, he has given up three earned runs over 10 ⅓ innings pitched, with his most recent start earning a win in the first game out of break against the Cubs. His command remains his calling card — his 18% K rate is modest, but the 6.5% walk rate is excellent, and he allows very little free traffic — though his pNERD of 2.64 reflects an xFIP- still in below-average territory. Cecconi's peripherals are similarly middling, edging Ober slightly on pNERD (3.51) thanks to youth and a bit of positive luck. Neither arm is a real building priority. entry.content:

Detail

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Los Angeles at Philadelphia is the best-scoring game on the board today, and it's got everything: a dominant ace fresh off surgery, a breakout lefty, and a Dodgers lineup nursing a hangover from getting torched the night before.

Zack Wheeler pairs a strong xFIP with excellent whiff rates, and his 8.75 pNERD ranks near the top of both today's and the historical pitcher pool. That's earned: Wheeler had thoracic outlet surgery last September, and his return this season has been nothing short of remarkable, posting a 2.13 ERA and 2.64 xERA in 15 starts with a 30.4-percent strikeout rate. He's been on an absolute tear lately, too — he blanked Detroit over six innings in his most recent outing, and has punched out double-digit batters in all three of his starts this month, totaling 34 strikeouts in 17 2/3 innings. Wrobleski isn't chopped liver either, coming off his first All-Star Game where he struck out five in two innings, tying a Dodgers record shared with Don Drysdale and Fernando Valenzuela. The Dodgers' 9.47 tNERD is elite, built on strong batting runs, barrel rate, and a deep bullpen, while Philadelphia's tNERD leans on a lively broadcast crew and a Trea Turner–powered offense that just dropped 10 runs on LA on Monday. With a 15.01 gNERD, this sits well above both the historical mean (10.11) and today's average (10.69) — arguably the day's marquee watch.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Good, I have enough to write the summary now.

Yankee Stadium hosts a fastball-vs-command puzzle box: Bubba Chandler's triple-digit heater is must-see, but you'll also see why he currently leads baseball in walks issued. This game rates a 12.58 gNERD, comfortably above the historical average of 10.11 and roughly in line with today's slate average of 10.69, driven almost entirely by two lively lineups rather than pitching artistry. The Yankees (8.77 tNERD) bring the majors' best AL slugging mark and a lineup led by Ben Rice's 29 home runs, while Pittsburgh (7.68 tNERD) counters with a surprisingly potent offense that's actually outscored New York by 63 runs this season despite the Yankees' better team ERA. Chandler leads all of baseball in walks issued and his 5.25 BB/9 is almost 100 points higher than the next pitcher, which explains his ugly 4.77 ERA despite a mid-90s-plus fastball that grades out as elite velocity in his pNERD profile (4.33). Will Warren (4.38 pNERD) is the steadier of the two, sporting a 7-4 record with a 4.03 ERA and 96 strikeouts over 98.1 innings, though his xFIP suggests he's actually pitched a bit better than his ERA shows. Expect fireworks, walks, and a scoreboard that won't sit still — this is watchable for the chaos, not the artistry.

New York Mets @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

A last-place team’s well-regarded rookie lefty against a division leader’s former farmhand who got dealt away in the same trade that just torched his old team — there’s a decent hook here even if the overall watchability is merely solid. Milwaukee (62-37, tops in the NL Central) rides a four-game winning streak into this one, and the Brewers rocked Freddy Peralta for seven runs in 5⅓ innings in Monday's series opener, with Andrew Vaughn and rookie Cooper Pratt going deep off him. Fittingly, Sproat was traded to Milwaukee in January along with Jett Williams in the deal that sent Peralta back to New York, and this marks his first start against his former squad. Sproat's pNERD (6.48) is buoyed by mid-90s velocity and a favorable luck reading, though his 24.7% strikeout rate is undercut by an 11.1% walk rate. Thornton gets a 0.00 pNERD for lack of data, but he's coming off seven scoreless innings against Boston, allowing two hits and two walks while throwing only 82 pitches — intriguing for a guy making just his fourth big-league start. The Brewers' tNERD (8.49) crushes New York's (4.13), pushing the gNERD to 12.05, comfortably above both the historic and today's averages.

Washington Nationals @ Colorado Rockies, 5:40p

Summary

Skip this one unless you just want to watch the Nationals mash dingers against a last-place team playing out the string. Washington's offense — majors-leading 147 home runs and MLB's highest-scoring attack — steamrolled Colorado 7-3 in the series opener, and the Rockies (40-62, worst record in baseball) are already selling off pieces like Seth Halvorsen ahead of the trade deadline, so this has more housekeeping-in-Denver vibes than drama.

The gNERD here is 7.81, sitting below both the historic median (10.11) and today's average (10.69), and that's almost entirely a lopsided tNERD split: Washington's 8.97 (young, athletic, good on the bases) against Colorado's paltry 1.31, dragged down by weak barrel rates and shaky fielding. The Nationals' bullpen, though, is a genuine sore spot — worst in the sport by our measure — so late innings could get messy in either direction.

On the mound, neither Mikolas (3.01 pNERD) nor Lorenzen (2.34) will wow you on paper, both carrying ERAs north of 5.50, but there's a wrinkle worth knowing: Mikolas has not allowed an earned run in four of his last seven outings and has struck out 14 while issuing just four walks in 38.0 innings since June 8, while Lorenzen struggled early in the season but has been steady in his last seven starts, going 1-1 with a 3.24 ERA, and has allowed just one home run in his past four outings. Modest stakes, modestly entertaining floor.

With a gNERD of 7.56, sitting below both the historic and today's averages, this one's more matinee filler than must-watch, unless you're partial to watching two last-place clubs sort out who's slightly less broken.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

This is about as good as it gets on the daily slate, with the Pirates’ ace-in-the-making squaring off against a Yankees lineup that never stops hitting. The 18.16 gNERD is the top mark of the day and creeps toward the all-time historic ceiling near 19.80, and it's easy to see why once you look at the roster sheets.

Braxton Ashcraft has quietly turned into Pittsburgh's best story of the season — he comes back from a stellar first half where he earned his first All-Star nod, posting a 9-3 record over 19 starts with a 3.43 ERA, 128 strikeouts against just 27 walks. His pNERD of 11.27 is buoyed by plus velocity, a stingy walk rate, and an xFIP- that suggests he's not just riding good fortune. Ryan Weathers isn't as flashy but still checks in with a solid 8.56 pNERD, thanks largely to a hefty luck bump — his ERA and results have run better than his peripherals suggest, so some regression could be lurking. The Yankees bring the sport's best barrel rate profile in this matchup, and both offenses rank near the top of the league in batting and baserunning value, making this a legitimately can't-miss ballgame.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Philadelphia Phillies, 4:10p

Summary

Good enough info. Let me write the summary.

Cristopher Sánchez is quietly having a Cy Young-caliber season, and this matchup pits the league's best record against arguably its stingiest arm. Sánchez enters at 11-4 with a 2.62 ERA, and his elite peripherals back it up — he's having an All-Star-caliber season: 11-4, a 2.62 ERA, 144 strikeouts — while he owns a 0.86 ERA and 61.9 GB% at home this season. His 10.02 pNERD is well above today's average and near the historic 95th percentile, driven by outstanding whiff and strike rates. Sheehan, by contrast, is homer-prone — solid strikeout numbers at 93, but he's been homer-prone, having already surrendered 15 long balls this season — though he did close the first half strong, striking out seven Diamondbacks over 5.1 innings in his last outing. The Dodgers carry MLB's best record but have scuffled lately, dropping three straight to a middling Diamondbacks club just over a week ago before salvaging a split at Yankee Stadium. With a 9.57 tNERD for LA (elite bullpen, fielding, and pop) and a well above-average 15.84 gNERD overall, this one lands comfortably above both the historic and today's-slate averages — worth carving out time for, mostly to watch Sánchez work.

New York Mets @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

I've got plenty here. Now writing the summary.

This one's a marquee pitching matchup wrapped in a revenge-game subplot, and the gNERD score backs it up as one of the best watches on the board today. Jacob Misiorowski returns from a bout of arm fatigue that scratched his final start before the break, and Milwaukee has posted a 10-4 record with a 1.62 ERA, 167 strikeouts, a 0.76 WHIP and a .148 opponents' batting average over 111 innings in his rookie season — the numbers behind a pNERD score near the top of today's slate, fueled by triple-digit velocity and elite whiff and strikeout rates. There's real juice here too: Freddy Peralta, the pitcher Milwaukee sent to New York in January in the trade that brought Sproat back, faces his former team for the first time, and Misiorowski is looking to erase his only prior appearance against New York, when he lasted just 3 2/3 innings, walked three and served up a grand slam to Brandon Nimmo. Peralta himself has been middling by his standards — a 4.66 ERA — and his pNERD reflects a modest profile, mostly propped up by decent luck regression upside. Milwaukee's tNERD is comfortably strong thanks to bullpen depth and a young, cheap roster, while the Mets' offense-starved lineup drags their side down. Historically, this game's overall score sits well above average, and the Misiorowski half alone is must-watch.

Good enough to work with. Now I'll draft the summary.

A four-game series with genuine stakes and a Padres team that's owned the Braves lately makes this opener worth a look, even if neither starter is likely to dazzle. San Diego enters having swept Atlanta in June and having won eight of their past nine against Atlanta dating to last season, and this "season-defining" set at Truist Park comes with the Padres reportedly heading toward being sellers, with the matchup telling the front office a lot about where this squad is for the remainder of the year. Atlanta, meanwhile, is trying to hold the NL East without Ronald Acuña Jr., who manager Walt Weiss said he wouldn't rule out returning during the series, as the 2023 NL MVP has been out since early June rehabbing a hamstring injury. On the mound, JP Sears carries no pNERD data to lean on and has been shaky, having allowed three runs on six hits over 4.1 innings in his last start against the Toronto Blue Jays, while Bryce Elder's modest 5.12 pNERD is buoyed mostly by a deliberate pace and youth rather than dominant stuff—his sub-92 mph velocity and below-average swinging-strike rate suggest more of a control-and-guile profile than a strikeout show. The real juice here comes from the offenses and bullpens: both pens rank well above average, and San Diego's tNERD of 9.12 is elite by today's standards (9.57 is the day's ceiling) thanks to strong baserunning, fielding, and broadcast appeal, while Atlanta's 7.04 still clears the historical average comfortably. With a combined gNERD of 13.14, sitting near the top of today's slate and well above the historical median, this one leans watchable on team quality and narrative more than on pitching artistry.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ New York Yankees, 9:35a

Summary

Good writeup opportunities. Now let me draft the summary.

A World Series preview, minus one Judge, plus a rain delay and a doubleheader — this is as good as the regular season gets. Yamamoto and Schlittler headline a gNERD score of 18.35, near the top of what you'll find today and comfortably in the upper crust historically. This rematch of the 2024 Fall Classic finds the Dodgers atop the NL West and the Yankees playing without Aaron Judge, and it comes as the makeup half of a doubleheader after Saturday's rainout in the Bronx. The Yankees are fielding their ace Cam Schlittler, the current frontrunner in midseason AL Cy Young polls, who has fully broken out following an impressive postseason performance in 2025. His pNERD of 9.80 backs that up, built on plus velocity, a low xFIP-, and a strikeout rate that's making hitters look silly. Yamamoto isn't far behind at 8.08, though he had a rough outing in his final start before the All-Star break, allowing six runs in six innings against the Diamondbacks, so he'll be looking to bounce back. Both offenses carry real thump — Ohtani and Rice among the game's top power threats — giving this the rare combination of ace pitching and lineup quality that actually deserves the hype.

Ace on the mound, missing star bat in the box, and a Pirates lineup that's finally scoring for once—this one's worth clicking on. Paul Skenes, the reigning NL Cy Young winner, headlines with a 10.18 pNERD (well above today's field, which averages 5.15), and the numbers back the eye test: Skenes has walked just 24 batters in over 108 innings this season, a command profile that's rare even among aces. He's also looking to bounce back after a rough stretch over the last two months, having been notably better in his last couple starts. Opposite him, Joey Cantillo (4.93 pNERD) is solid but unspectacular, with shakier control—49 walks in 101 innings—and he'll do it without Cleveland's best hitter, as Jose Ramirez's absence removes Cleveland's best all-around hitter from the middle of the order. Both lineups carry decent tNERD marks (7.52 and 7.32), lifted by baserunning and, for Cleveland, a young, cheap roster. Combined gNERD of 14.97 sits comfortably above both the historic 95th percentile (14.76) and today's average (11.00)—a genuinely well-built matchup, ace edge and all.

A near-perfect game encore and a Brewers club with the best record in baseball make this one worth clearing your schedule for. Eury Pérez, the 23-year-old flamethrower who missed two months with a gracilis strain, came back and threw seven innings toward a perfect game on July 5, retiring all 21 batters he faced on 92 pitches, before being taken out. His pNERD of 7.59 is well above today's 5.15 average, driven by elite velocity (98.1 mph) and a swinging-strike rate that ranks near the top of the league. The Marlins, once assumed sellers, have instead been baseball's best team since the beginning of June, reeling off a 24-8 stretch, and it shows in their tNERD of 9.73 — youth, baserunning, and a modest payroll all pulling their weight. Milwaukee counters with a stacked bullpen and its own tNERD of 8.30, riding a young, cheap roster to the league's best record. Robert Gasser is the weaker link on the mound, with an xFIP- of 112 pulling his pNERD down to 4.23, though a positive luck figure suggests his results have been a bit worse than his stuff deserves.
